numerical_failure.observed_behavior: When the flat-index inputs are provided as an (8194, 1) array (derived from np.arange(8194)), np.unravel_index returns incorrect column coordinates for flat index 8193: returned coordinate is (8, 192) instead of (8, 193). The round-trip via np.ravel_multi_index of (row_2d, col_2d) then returns 8192 instead of the original 8193, causing a mismatch (1 element mismatched out of 8194).
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: For flat index 8193, np.unravel_index should return (row, col) = (8, 193). Then np.ravel_multi_index((row, col), (1000, 1000)) should round-trip back to 8193. More generally, for the same flat indices represented as (8194,) vs (8194, 1), the returned row/col coordinates and the round-tripped indices should be identical.
trigger_conditions: Using np.unravel_index on an array of flat indices with shape (8194,) works correctly, but using the same flat indices stored in an (8194, 1) array produces a round-trip mismatch.
The discrepancy occurs at flat index 8193 (first mismatch position: 8193) with 2-D input shape (8194, 1).

Example failing case uses shape (1000, 1000), flat indices up to 8193 (indices_1d = np.arange(first_bad+1) with first_bad=8193), dtype np.intp/int64, and 2-D input is C-contiguous with strides (8, 8).

input_output_examples.input: indices_1d = np.arange(8194, dtype=np.intp); indices_2d = indices_1d[:, None]; shape = (1000, 1000); row_2d, col_2d = np.unravel_index(indices_2d, shape) at pos=8193 (so indices_1d[pos]=8193)
input_output_examples.buggy_output: For pos=8193: 2-D returned coordinate (row_2d[pos,0], col_2d[pos,0]) = (8, 192); 2-D round-tripped value restored_2d[pos,0] = 8192.
input_output_examples.expected_output: For pos=8193: expected coordinate (expected_row_1d[pos], expected_col_1d[pos]) = (8, 193); expected 2-D round-tripped value restored_2d[pos,0] = 8193.

oracle_clues: Correctness is judged by round-trip equality: restored_2d = np.ravel_multi_index((row_2d, col_2d), shape) should equal indices_2d (then also restored_2d.ravel() should equal indices_1d).
The failing run reports: "Number of round-trip mismatches for 2-D input: 1" and "First mismatch position: 8193".
The coordinate oracle for the mismatch uses expected_row_1d = indices_1d // shape[1] and expected_col_1d = indices_1d % shape[1], and at pos=8193 expects (8, 193) rather than (8, 192).
An assertion is used: np.testing.assert_array_equal(restored_2d, indices_2d) (fails with "Arrays are not equal" and "Mismatched elements: 1 / 8194").

provenance.value: For flat index 8193, when represented as an (N, 1) input array shape (8194, 1), the returned unravel coordinates (row,col) are (8,192) instead of (8,193); the subsequent round-trip via ravel_multi_index returns 8192 instead of 8193. Output comparison fails with an assertion that arrays are not equal (mismatch at exactly 1 element).

For flat index 8193, the returned unravel coordinates should be (8,193), and ravel_multi_index of those coordinates should round-trip back to 8193. In the example, desired coordinate values end with ..., 192, 193 rather than ..., 191, 192, 192.
8194-length 1-D input and (8194, 1) 2-D input; flat index mismatch at 8193

When the flat-index inputs are provided as an (8194, 1) array (derived from np.arange(8194)), np.unravel_index returns incorrect column coordinates for flat index 8193: returned coordinate is (8, 192) instead of (8, 193). The round-trip via np.ravel_multi_index of (row_2d, col_2d) then returns 8192 instead of the original 8193, causing a mismatch (1 element mismatched out of 8194).

For flat index 8193, np.unravel_index should return (row, col) = (8, 193). Then np.ravel_multi_index((row, col), (1000, 1000)) should round-trip back to 8193. More generally, for the same flat indices represented as (8194,) vs (8194, 1), the returned row/col coordinates and the round-tripped indices should be identical.
